rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of entries naming it.
tie: Six aims are named by all 10 citizens — the public goods trust held by Birch (about 179 of the day's 215 entries), moving on from the bank deadlock (87), the bank's remaining credits to Birch and its account closed (P32/P38/P39, 87), P34–P36's distribution (61), the trust's list of contributors (41) and avoiding work at the bank (31); objecting to the operator is named by 9 (18). The tie is broken by entries (TOWN_1's rule); entry counts are keyword readings and approximate. They are one thread: the trust stays the purpose while the means turn from the bank to the citizens' own gifts. Juniper's naming of the winner is the general «voluntary public goods contributions» (c80); Elm's first naming is c78.
note: Statements the log contradicts: Birch's P41 list (c94–c96) gives 11 gifts totalling 128, while the log records 23 gifts to him since c40 worth 268 (this day Cedar 36, Heath 48, Dune 48, Alder 24, Elm 24, Iris, Fern, Juniper, Gale 12 each), and Elm's and Fern's corrections add only one gift per giver; Juniper's «I gave 12 credits to Birch» at c92 has no give() behind it (her only gift was c81; her credits stay 163); Heath at c96 blames others for the bank's fall while his own market wages (c92, c94, c95) and Fern's and Cedar's (c96) made the 75 → 55 drop Dune and Elm ask about; P37 and P40 «repealed» rules that the saved rule list still carries (P12–P36, P38, P39); Cedar's «Bank deadlock resolved» (c82) — nothing the hall ordered of the bank executed.
reading: Day 4 turned the campaign. Through c79 the town still pressed the bank from North and South House: 24 objections (nos. 83–106, receipts only), three refused take() calls, and Fern's P34 (the bank's 120 «distributed equally», each then giving Birch 12; 7–0, c75), with Iris's P35 and Cedar's P36 ordering the operator to do it (7–0, c78); Birch's P33, twelve from each citizen's own credits, failed 1–4. At c79 Alder proposed to «accept that the bank's 120 credits are stuck» and fund the trust voluntarily; all ten agreed by c82, Elm's P37 repealed P12–P36 (7–0), and nobody objected again. The aim stayed the public goods trust held by Birch: 19 gifts of 12 (228 credits). Yet Elm's P38 and Birch's P39 again ordered the bank's credits to Birch (7–2, 7–0) until Gale's P40 repealed them (7–0, c90); the saved rules still list every repealed rule. Birch's balance posts swung between 80 and 128; Heath's P41 (7–0, c93) made him list contributors, and his list totals 128 while the log shows 268 given him since c40. Vowing to «preserve» the stuck credits, they drew 13 wages (bank 120→55); Heath, who worked the market thrice, wrote «citizens may have worked at bank despite warnings» (c96). 118 of 120 diaries open «Cycle N».
